claim: Dm ECT2 localized rapidly to cortical sites contacted by MT plus-tips.

claim: MT plus-tip contact by Dm ECT2 results in RhoA activation.

claim: MT plus-tip contact by Dm ECT2 results in enrichment of myosin-regulatory light chain.

claim: Centralspindlin plus-tip localization depended on a putative EB1-interaction motif (hxxPTxh) in RacGAP50C.

source: Cell division ends with the formation of an actomyosin contractile ring, positioned midway between the segregated chromosomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge in cell biology cited in the introduction.

source: Constriction of the ring generates a cleavage furrow that physically divides the cytosol, a process known as cytokinesis.
evidence: This is a definition and established knowledge in cell biology.

source: Establishing and maintaining the position of the cleavage furrow between daughter nuclei is vital for embryonic development, tissue and stem cell maintenance, and preserving ploidy (Li, 2007).

source: In animal cells, the spindle apparatus specifies the position of the cleavage furrow during anaphase (Rappaport, 1961), and it is widely accepted that the cleavage plane is positioned via microtubule (MT)-dependent mechanisms (Rappaport, 1996)

claim: Centralspindlin is a tetrameric complex consisting of a dimer of the kinesin-6 family member MKLP1 bound to a dimer of the GTPase activating protein MgcRacGAP/Cyk4.

claim: Centralspindlin is a robust MT bundler.
source: Centralspindlin is a robust MT bundler and following anaphase onset the complex becomes highly enriched in MT overlaps.
evidence: This is established knowledge about centralspindlin function.

claim: Following anaphase onset the centralspindlin complex becomes highly enriched in MT overlaps.
source: Centralspindlin is a robust MT bundler and following anaphase onset the complex becomes highly enriched in MT overlaps.

evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The relative functional contributions of the various pools of centralspindlin to furrow positioning are poorly understood.
source: The relative functional contributions of the various pools of centralspindlin to furrow positioning are poorly understood.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

source: Spatio-temporal regulation of cytokinesis is also controlled by a complex interplay of cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1), Aurora B kinase (ABK), and Polo kinase.

source: High CDK1 activity during mitosis results in phosphorylation of the centralspindlin component MKLP1, which prevents its association with MTs until after anaphase onset as CDK1 activity drops (Glotzer, 2009; Mishima et al., 2004).

claim: Binding and enrichment of MKLP1 on the central spindle is regulated by ABK activity, which stabilizes the midzone localization of the centralspindlin complex via phosphorylation of MKLP1.
source: Binding and enrichment of MKLP1 on the central spindle is further regulated by ABK activity, which stabilizes the midzone localization of the centralspindlin complex via phosphorylation of MKLP1 (Douglas et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Douglas et al., 2010.

claim: In many cell types, midzone localization of the ABK-containing chromosomal passenger complex (CPC) is dependent on the plus-end directed motor MKLP2.
source: In many cell types, midzone localization of the ABK-containing chromosomal passenger complex (CPC) is dependent on the plus-end directed motor MKLP2 (Cesario et al., 2006; Gruneberg et al., 2004; Kitagawa et al., 2013; Nguyen et al., 2014)

claim: ABK's cortical localization depends on actin binding by the CPC component INCENP.

source: While the role of ABK at the central spindle is well documented, its function at the equatorial cortex has not been extensively examined

claim: Polo kinase plays a central role in cytokinesis.
source: Polo kinase also plays a central role in cytokinesis (Brennan et al., 2007; Burkard et al., 2009; Carmena et al., 2014; Llamazares et al., 1991; Petronczki et al., 2008).

claim: Polo kinase phosphorylates the centralspindlin component RacGAP50C to recruit the RhoGEF, ECT2, to the midzone.
source: Polo kinase phosphorylates the centralspindlin component RacGAP50C (Ebrahimi et al., 2010), to recruit the RhoGEF, ECT2, to the midzone (Burkard et al., 2009; Petronczki et al., 2007; Somers and Saint, 2003; Wolfe et al., 2009).

claim: ECT2 produces RhoA-GTP at the membrane, which promotes cortical contractility via activation of downstream actin and myosin regulatory pathways.
source: ECT2 produces RhoA-GTP at the membrane, which promotes cortical contractility via activation of downstream actin and myosin regulatory pathways (Bement et al., 2005; Jordan and Canman, 2012; Yüce et al., 2005).

claim: PRC1 (Feo in Drosophila) and Kinesin-4 (Klp3A in Drosophila) are required for Polo kinase recruitment to the midzone in Drosophila and mammalian cells.
source: PRC1 (Feo in Drosophila) and Kinesin-4 (Klp3A in Drosophila) are required for Polo kinase recruitment to the midzone in Drosophila and mammalian cells (D'Avino et al., 2007; Neef et al., 2007).

source: However, Feo depletion does not result in cleavage furrow initiation or ingression defects (D'Avino et al., 2007), indicating that midzone-localized Polo is not necessary for furrow positioning.

claim: Midzone-localized Polo is not necessary for furrow positioning.
source: However, Feo depletion does not result in cleavage furrow initiation or ingression defects (D'Avino et al., 2007), indicating that midzone-localized Polo is not necessary for furrow positioning.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited work of D'Avino et al., 2007.

claim: Global Polo kinase activity is essential for cytokinesis as it is required for cleavage furrow initiation.
source: Nevertheless, global Polo kinase activity is essential for cytokinesis as it is required for cleavage furrow initiation (Brennan et al., 2007; Lénárt et al., 2007; Petronczki et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brennan et al., 2007; Lénárt et al., 2007; Petronczki et al., 2007.

claim: Live-cell imaging revealed that centralspindlin (Dm MKLP1 and RacGAP50C), ABK, and Polo each localize to and track astral MT plus-tips within minutes of anaphase onset.
source: Live-cell imaging revealed that centralspindlin (Dm MKLP1 and RacGAP50C), ABK, and Polo each localize to and track astral MT plus-tips within minutes of anaphase onset before being lost from a majority of polar astral MTs and retained on equatorial astral MTs.

claim: Centralspindlin, ABK, and Polo are lost from a majority of polar astral MTs and retained on equatorial astral MTs.
source: Live-cell imaging revealed that centralspindlin (Dm MKLP1 and RacGAP50C), ABK, and Polo each localize to and track astral MT plus-tips within minutes of anaphase onset before being lost from a majority of polar astral MTs and retained on equatorial astral MTs.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study shown in Figure 1 and Videos 2-4.

claim: Specialized MT plus-tips enriched with centralspindlin were deemed 'cytokinesis signaling TIPs' (CS-TIPs) because they recruited cortical ECT2 and locally activated RhoA.
source: Specialized MT plus-tips enriched with centralspindlin were deemed ''cytokinesis signaling TIPs'', referred to hereafter as CS-TIPs, because they recruited cortical ECT2 and locally activated RhoA.

claim: 97% of dividing cells began to ingress furrows in the mid-cell region within ~10 min of anaphase onset on Con A.
source: Importantly, we found that 97% of dividing cells began to ingress furrows in the mid-cell region within ~10 min of anaphase onset.

claim: 32% of cells on Con A completed cytokinesis normally.
source: Of these cells, 32% completed cytokinesis normally (as defined by clearly delineated mono-nucleated daughter cells) while 68% of cells regressed their furrows 39.4 ± 7.6 min. after furrow ingression initiated (Video 1, n = 28, mean ± SD values are reported).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from overnight time-lapse imaging shown in Video 1.

claim: 68% of cells on Con A regressed their furrows 39.4 ± 7.6 min. after furrow ingression initiated.
source: Of these cells, 32% completed cytokinesis normally (as defined by clearly delineated mono-nucleated daughter cells) while 68% of cells regressed their furrows 39.4 ± 7.6 min. after furrow ingression initiated (Video 1, n = 28, mean ± SD values are reported).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from overnight time-lapse imaging shown in Video 1.

claim: The Con A concentration used in these experiments negatively impacted the latest stages of cytokinesis (most likely cytokinetic abscission) but did not affect the processes of cleavage furrow establishment and ingression.
source: Thus, the Con A concentration used in these experiments negatively impacted the latest stages of cytokinesis (most likely cytokinetic abscission) but did not affect the processes that we aimed to study, namely cleavage furrow establishment and ingression.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data from Video 1 and the quantification of cytokinesis outcomes.

claim: In metaphase, Dm MKLP1 diffusely localized throughout the cytosol without evident spindle MT enrichment.
source: In metaphase, Dm MKLP1 diffusely localized throughout the cytosol without evident spindle MT enrichment (Video 2)
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging shown in Video 2.

claim: Dm MKLP1 localized to astral MT plus-tips, both polar and equatorial, before being lost from the polar tips and becoming preferentially patterned onto equatorial tips ~ 10 min. following anaphase onset.

claim: RacGAP50C exhibited MT plus-end localization and tip-tracking activity during cytokinesis.
source: In agreement with a recent report of MgcRacGAP localization to the MT plus-ends in Xenopus laevis (Breznau et al., 2017), we also observed MT plus-end localization and tip-tracking activity of RacGAP50C during cytokinesis (Figure 1B; Video 3)
evidence: This is a primary observation from live-cell TIRF microscopy shown in Figure 1B and Video 3.

claim: RacGAP50C decorated polar and equatorial astral MT plus-ends within ~2 min. of anaphase onset before becoming patterned onto equatorial MTs.
source: Like Dm MKLP1, RacGAP50C decorated polar and equatorial astral MT plus-ends within ~2 min. of anaphase onset before becoming patterned onto equatorial MTs.
evidence: This is a primary observation from live-cell TIRF microscopy shown in Figure 1B and Video 3.

claim: RacGAP50C and Dm MKLP1 accumulated on midzone MTs and the equatorial cortex.
source: We also observed RacGAP50C and Dm MKLP1 accumulation on midzone MTs and the equatorial cortex (Figure 1A,B; Videos 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a primary observation from live-cell TIRF microscopy shown in Figure 1A-B and Videos 2-3.

claim: The two components of the centralspindlin complex, Dm MKLP1 and RacGAP50C, exhibit the same dynamic localization pattern on midzone MTs, the cortex, and astral MT plus-tips as cells progressed through anaphase and cytokinesis.
source: Thus, the two components of the centralspindlin complex, Dm MKLP1 and RacGAP50C, exhibit the same dynamic localization pattern on midzone MTs, the cortex, and astral MT plus-tips as cells progressed through anaphase and cytokinesis.

claim: The Dm MKLP1-EGFP transgene was expressed ~5 fold lower than its endogenous counterpart.
source: Western blotting indicated that the Dm MKLP1-EGFP transgene was expressed ~5 fold lower than its endogenous counterpart (Figure 1C).

claim: Dm MKLP1-EGFP localized to MT plus-ends, midzones, and the cortex when endogenous Dm MKLP1 was depleted.
source: Importantly, Dm MKLP1-EGFP localized to MT plus-ends, midzones, and the cortex when endogenous Dm MKLP1 was depleted and rescued the severe cytokinesis failure phenotype that resulted from depletion of Dm MKLP1. (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: Dm MKLP1-EGFP rescued the severe cytokinesis failure phenotype that resulted from depletion of Dm MKLP1.
source: Importantly, Dm MKLP1-EGFP localized to MT plus-ends, midzones, and the cortex when endogenous Dm MKLP1 was depleted and rescued the severe cytokinesis failure phenotype that resulted from depletion of Dm MKLP1. (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from RNAi rescue experiments shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: CS-TIPs are not restricted to the ventral surface of the cell as the decoration of CS-TIPs was observed throughout the cell volume (up to 4.6 µm towards the dorsal surface).

claim: RacGAP50C-EGFP expression was less than its endogenous counterpart.
source: Like Dm MKLP1-EGFP, RacGAP50C-EGFP expression was less than its endogenous counterpart (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from western blotting shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of RacGAP50C-EGFP largely rescued the failure of cytokinesis following RacGAP50C depletion.
source: Expression of RacGAP50C-EGFP largely rescued the failure of cytokinesis following RacGAP50C depletion and the RacGAP50C-EGFP localized to CS-TIPs, midzones, and the cortex when the endogenous RacGAP50C was depleted (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from RNAi rescue experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: RacGAP50C-EGFP localized to CS-TIPs, midzones, and the cortex when the endogenous RacGAP50C was depleted.
source: Expression of RacGAP50C-EGFP largely rescued the failure of cytokinesis following RacGAP50C depletion and the RacGAP50C-EGFP localized to CS-TIPs, midzones, and the cortex when the endogenous RacGAP50C was depleted (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from RNAi rescue experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The spatio-temporal properties of the MT plus-tip population of centralspindlin were not a consequence of transgene overexpression.
source: Altogether, these data lead us to conclude that the spatio-temporal properties of the MT plus-tip population of centralspindlin were not a consequence of transgene overexpression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the western blotting and RNAi rescue experiments shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ABK localized on polar and equatorial astral MT plus-tips, midzones, and the equatorial cortex.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Landino et al., 2017; Vale et al., 2009), we also observed ABK localization on polar and equatorial astral MT plus-tips, midzones, and the equatorial cortex (Figure 1E).

claim: Polo kinase activity is required for furrow initiation and successful cytokinesis.
source: Polo kinase becomes enriched on midzones during cytokinesis and its activity is required for furrow initiation and successful cytokinesis (Brennan et al., 2007; Burkard et al., 2009; Carmena et al., 1998; Lénárt et al., 2007; Petronczki et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Polo localized to the overlap zone of the midzone MT array.

evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging, consistent with prior work cited.

claim: Polo kinase localizes to interphase MTs in Drosophila cells.
source: Polo kinase uniformly localized along the length of MTs as cells advanced into late telophase, which was expected since Polo kinase localizes to interphase MTs in Drosophila cells (Archambault et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Archambault et al., 2008.

claim: In cells expressing Polo-EGFP, inward moving zones of Polo-EGFP exclusion were often observed.
source: In cells expressing Polo-EGFP we often observed inward moving zones of Polo-EGFP exclusion (Figure 1G; Video 4).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging shown in Figure 1G and Video 4.

claim: MTs could not penetrate Polo-EGFP exclusion zones and were pushed inward as the zones expanded.
source: Since MTs could not penetrate these exclusion zones and were pushed inward as the zones expanded, we interpreted the Polo-EGFP exclusion zones as indicative of local regions of actomyosin contractility.
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging shown in Figure 1G and Video 4.

claim: Polo-EGFP exclusion zones are indicative of local regions of actomyosin contractility.
source: Since MTs could not penetrate these exclusion zones and were pushed inward as the zones expanded, we interpreted the Polo-EGFP exclusion zones as indicative of local regions of actomyosin contractility.
